## Looking for Scholarships? Sallie Shares 5 Ways Students and Families Can Maximize Free Money for College


11/23/2026


Download this Press Release PDF Format (opens in new window)


*Simple Tips Can Help Students and Families Find More Opportunities and Avoid Missing Out on Free Money for College*


NEWARK, Del.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Nearly 8 in 10 families who used scholarships in the 2025-26 academic year said that money helped make college possible, according to Sallie’s[How America Pays for College 2026](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.salliemae.com%2Fabout%2Fleading-research%2Fhow-america-pays-for-college%2F&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=How+America+Pays+for+College+2026&index=1&md5=349ccf26d6bf9d9c7ee87e3aa69f8c04) . This National Scholarship Month,[Sallie](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=Sallie&index=2&md5=d4ddea73dbc7221ea6e8fe4a3cfd2ca9) is dispelling myths and misconceptions about scholarships to help students and families access free money that can make college affordable.


That’s particularly important given nearly half (48%) of families believe[scholarships](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fscholarships&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=scholarships&index=3&md5=c22499458b4170847cd23c07641d5773) are only reserved for students with exceptional grades or abilities, 41% think they are only available to incoming freshmen, and 35% believe their family’s income is too high to qualify. The reality is scholarships are available for a wide variety of interests and backgrounds, more than half are available for current college students, and[not all](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fscholarships%2Fguide%2Fcommon-requirements&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=not+all&index=4&md5=5493037cc631c4c27b716e62f289cbdf) are based on financial need. Whether students are just starting their search or are actively applying, Sallie has tips to help students and families find and make the most of scholarship opportunities:


1. **Apply early and often.** Scholarships are available throughout the higher education journey. Start early in high school and keep applying throughout college and[graduate school](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fscholarships%2Ftypes%2Fgraduate-students&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=graduate+school&index=5&md5=7060ae48228c5cb5b6eb25b2739e61d9) .
2. **Turn interests into opportunities** . Scholarships can[reward interests you might not expect](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fresources%2Fscholarships%2Fhidden-lesser-known&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=reward+interests+you+might+not+expect&index=6&md5=3ba56f8ee151d224c51dbc4fda3ad180) . In fact, there are[unique scholarships](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fresources%2Fscholarships%2Funique-scholarships&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=unique+scholarships&index=7&md5=c9284c81315713aa86d6b4278349eb91) for interests like hat design, bass fishing, designing greeting cards, skateboarding, and even potato farming. Students should think about the hobbies and interests they enjoy and use them to guide their search.
3. **Don’t overlook**[smaller award opportunities](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fresearch%2Fthe-scholarship-winner-playbook&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=smaller+award+opportunities&index=8&md5=9c0758d6385678a80495f1a867cfe943) **.** Higher-dollar scholarships also bring bigger competition, but[smaller awards](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fscholarships%2Fguide&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=smaller+awards&index=9&md5=7c9e89a606f0773e05b97c2a1faabe6c) can add up and make a difference. A few hundred dollars can help cover books, supplies, and other college costs beyond tuition and room and board.
4. **Use a mix of sources.** Start with your school counselor or financial aid office, then widen your search. Check with employers, community groups, professional organizations, and[other local groups](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fresources%2Fscholarships%2Flocal-scholarships-guide&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=other+local+groups&index=10&md5=ff28c4a963964cabf4903f9bb403e6ca) . Taking the time to explore different opportunities and putting together a strong application can pay off.
5. **Make every application count.** Research the organization behind each award, check eligibility and deadlines, and tailor your response to the specific application. Sallie[found that scholarship winners](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fresearch%2Fthe-scholarship-winner-playbook&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=found+that+scholarship+winners&index=11&md5=f9a630884274f193c4c8d492f98d5c1e) were more likely to research the organization before writing and nearly 1 in 4 had their essays reviewed regularly by another person.


“Tapping into scholarships is one of the most effective ways to make college more affordable, but too often families are unclear on what’s available, if they’ll qualify, or where to even look,” said Rick Castellano, vice president,[Sallie](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2F&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=Sallie&index=12&md5=222f3058022d20643b694b0939aea763) . “The good news is there are free resources like Scholly that simplify the scholarship search. Free money for college is out there so start early, apply often, and don’t count yourself out.”


**More Ways Sallie Supports Students**


Beyond free tools and resources that help students and families find scholarships, The Sallie Mae Fund provides additional scholarship opportunities through its[Bridging the Dream Scholarship Program](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.salliemae.com%2Flanding%2Fbridging-the-dream%2F&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=Bridging+the+Dream+Scholarship+Program&index=13&md5=a161540728fc6639989d94cd218a0611) and[Completing the Dream Scholarship](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.salliemae.com%2Flanding%2Fcompleting-the-dream%2F&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=Completing+the+Dream+Scholarship&index=14&md5=c8e244be10e5aac41e30d6a3243993d4) . Since 2021, the programs have awarded more than $5.5 million in scholarships to nearly 1,500 students across the country. Sallie also offers a suite of[planning tools and resources](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.salliemae.com%2Fresources%2F%3Fdtd_cell%3Dsmccmpsccmocototothothrn030000%26utm_campaign%3Dcc_u_u_u_u_b_pros_b%26utm_source%3Dbw%26utm_medium%3Dpr%26utm_content%3Dpressrelease.html&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=planning+tools+and+resources&index=15&md5=23f4f03e09a51411a32087d8178e82b9) to help students and families plan and responsibly pay for college.


For free scholarship and college planning resources, visit[Sallie.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sallie.com%2Fscholarships&esheet=54645578&newsitemid=20261123556103&lan=en-US&anchor=Sallie.com&index=16&md5=dff02e913b8c41fcd5cbf86cba6dc5c3) .

As the leader in private student lending, we provide financing and know-how to support access to college and offer products and resources to help customers make new goals and experiences, beyond college, happen.
